name: Murkfiend Liege
oracle_text:
Other green creatures you control get +1/+1.
Other blue creatures you control get +1/+1.
Untap all green and/or blue creatures you control during each other player's untap step.
blocked_sentences: Untap all green and/or blue creatures you control during each other player's untap step.
scope: ONLY the third line is blocked. Both anthem lines are fully expressible today with vocabulary already in the packet's `reference` block -- see `expressible_today` below, recorded so nobody re-triages them and so whoever clears the untap line can write the whole card in one pass. The card goes here rather than being written half because a partly-expressible card is a gap record by the brief, and because the untap line is not decoration: it is the entire reason Murkfiend Liege is played over any other five-mana lord. A version with only the two anthems is a strictly worse card than the one printed, and it would read as finished on the board.

needs.what: A continuous ability, read by the untap-step turn-based action, that adds a set of permanents chosen by an ordinary static filter to the set untapped during a *different* player's untap step. Concretely a static of the shape `{"kind": "static", "effect": "untap_during_others_untap_step", "affects": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "colors": ["G", "U"]}}`, and a matching read inside `primitives.untap_all` (`src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:437-460`): today it walks the battlefield and skips every object whose `controller != pid`, so it must additionally untap any object matched by an active static of this kind whose controller is not the active player. The filter is the existing static selector (`characteristics._matches` -> the selector walk at `characteristics.py:270-300`), where `colors` is already an intersection test -- `if colors and not (set(colors) & card.colors)` at line 284-286 -- so `["G", "U"]` means exactly the printed "green and/or blue". This one effect covers the whole family at once: Seedborn Muse, Prophet of Kruphix, Awakening, Murkfiend Liege and Vedalken Orrery-adjacent 'untaps during each untap step' text all differ only in the filter.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_effects` is limited to `buff`, `grant_keyword`, `set_pt`, `add_subtype` and `extra_land_drops`. The first four write characteristics that the characteristics pipeline reads; `extra_land_drops` writes a player permission that the land-play legality check reads. None of them is read anywhere near the untap step. `skip_untap` is the closest existing vocabulary -- it is the *only* thing in the reference block that touches the untap step at all -- and it is the exact negation of what is wanted: it sets a one-shot `skip_next_untap` flag on an object, consumed by `untap_all` (`primitives.py:450-455`) to *remove* a permanent from an untap it would otherwise get. There is no positive counterpart, and no amount of skipping can add a permanent to an untap step that never considered it: `untap_all` is called from `turn._untap_step` (`turn.py:110-118`) as `untap_all(state, player.pid)` with the active player's pid hard-wired, so permanents controlled by anyone else are filtered out before any flag is consulted.

needs.what: An `untap_step` trigger event, fired for the untapping player and honouring the existing `controller: "opponent"` clause, plus priority plumbing so an ability that triggers there can actually resolve during that step. This is the near-miss route -- 'at the beginning of each other player's untap step, untap all green and/or blue creatures you control' -- and it is written down because it is the first thing anyone will reach for; see below for why it is second best even once it exists.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Three separate stops, all verified in the source. (1) There is no event: `TRIGGER_EVENTS` (`src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:28-47`) maps `upkeep`, `draw_step`, `begin_combat` and `end_step` and nothing for the untap step. (2) Nothing is even emitted for triggers to match: `turn.begin_step` handles `Step.UNTAP` by calling `_untap_step`, which uses `state.emit(EventType.TURN_BEGAN, ...)` rather than `triggers.fire(...)` (`turn.py:34-35`, `110-118`) -- `emit` records the event but never calls `collect`, so no ability is scanned during that step, and `TURN_BEGAN` is not in `TRIGGER_EVENTS` either. (3) Even with both fixed, the timing would be wrong: `step_grants_priority` returns `False` for `Step.UNTAP` (`turn.py:186-189`, correct per rule 502.3), so a queued triggered ability would sit in `pending_triggers` until the upkeep and untap one step late -- and worse, it would be respondable, which the printed card is not. Murkfiend Liege's line is a static ability modifying a turn-based action, not a trigger; the `static_effect` need above is the shape that matches the card. `delay` cannot stand in either: its `DELAY_STEPS` whitelist (`turn.py:68-73`) has no untap entry, and a delayed trigger is one-shot and must be scheduled by something that already resolved, whereas this is a permanent, always-on modification of every other player's untap step.

expressible_today.note: Both anthem lines need NO new vocabulary. `colors` is a printed characteristic and a legal `static_filter_keys` entry, and the selector's colour test is an intersection, so `colors: ["G"]` correctly matches a gold green-blue creature. `exclude_self` covers the printed word 'Other' -- Murkfiend Liege is itself both green and blue, so without it the card would pump itself twice.

abilities.text: Other green creatures you control get +1/+1.
Other blue creatures you control get +1/+1.

expressible_today.why_two_abilities_and_not_one: `colors: ["G", "U"]` in a single buff would be a *different card*: the selector's colour test is an OR, so one +1/+1 would reach every green-or-blue creature, whereas the printed card gives a creature that is both green and blue +2/+2. Two statics stack correctly on such a creature and each claims its own printed line, which is also what the residual gate wants.
expressible_today.expectation_if_the_card_were_written: `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}` and nothing more. The sandbox's two creatures are chosen by role, not colour, so neither their colours nor their printed P/T can be assumed, and there is no expectation key that reads the P/T of a permanent that is not the spell's own target -- `target_pt_delta` only applies to a spell that targeted, and this card targets nothing. The untap line cannot be observed either: the harness casts the card in the controller's own precombat main phase and stops, so no other player's untap step is ever reached.
